channel.title: The Philosophers' Magazine - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Philosophers' Magazine (philosophersmag.com)

item.title: Cribs and Hunters - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: E. E. Sheng considers the meteoric rise of the notion of self-plagiarism.

item.title: 45 Years of French Philosophy - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Vincent Descombes looks back on his history of French philosophy from 1933 to 1978.

item.title: A Just-So Story - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Pascal Engel critically reviews 'A Social History of Analytic Philosophy' by Christoph Schuringa.

item.title: A Dangerous Idea - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Felice Basbøll reviews "What is Free Speech? A Dangerous Idea and Its History" by Fara Dabhoiwala.

item.title: An Air of Unreality - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: The Gazan genocide narrative is obviously false, argues Russell Blackford.

item.title: The Gender-Based Rights Conundrum - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Rona Dinur argues that trans/gender activism was never about protecting anyone's rights.

item.title: Beneath the Surface of Straussianism - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Oliver Traldi argues that Straussianism is an impoverished approach to philosophical education.

item.title: A Visit to Königsberg-Kaliningrad - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: On the tercentenary of Kant’s birth, 22 April 2024, J. L. H. Thomas recalls a visit to Königsberg-Kaliningrad.

item.title: Jihadism: At Least as Bad as Nazism - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Spencer Case provides three reasons that jihadism is at least as bad as Nazism.

item.title: On Being Rejected - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: First a review article, then a book, now a book review—Alex Byrne chronicles the latest surprise rejection of his writing in the philosophy of sex and gender.

item.title: Living with Class - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Hanno Sauer argues that we will have to learn how to live with class hierarchy.

item.title: The Problem with Everything - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Daniel Kodsi and John Maier argue that all battles in the culture wars depend on the same philosophical mistake.

item.title: The Ethics of Sex Verification - The Philosophers' Magazine
item.description: Miroslav Imbrišević and Jon Pike argue that it is justified to treat different cases differently in sports.
